In [5]:
# ============================================================
# FINAL MODEL DATA CONSTRUCTION
# ============================================================

# Start directly from research_sample
# Do NOT drop missing rows yet

model_data = research_sample[
    [
        "MKT_RF",
        "SMB",
        "HML",
        "RMW",
        "CMA",
        "MOM",
        "RF",

        "VIX",
        "Credit_Spread",
        "Term_Spread",
        "Treasury_2Y",
        "Inflation",
        "Unemployment",
        "IP_Growth"
    ]
].copy()


# ============================================================
# 1. CREATE LAGGED MACRO VARIABLES
# ============================================================

model_data["Inflation_lag1"] = (
    model_data["Inflation"].shift(1)
)

model_data["Unemployment_lag1"] = (
    model_data["Unemployment"].shift(1)
)

model_data["IP_Growth_lag1"] = (
    model_data["IP_Growth"].shift(1)
)


# ============================================================
# 2. CREATE NEXT-MONTH FACTOR TARGETS
# ============================================================

factor_columns = [
    "MKT_RF",
    "SMB",
    "HML",
    "RMW",
    "CMA",
    "MOM"
]

for factor in factor_columns:

    model_data[f"{factor}_next"] = (
        model_data[factor].shift(-1)
    )


# ============================================================
# 3. DEFINE PREDICTOR VARIABLES
# ============================================================

predictor_columns = [
    "VIX",
    "Credit_Spread",
    "Term_Spread",
    "Treasury_2Y",
    "Inflation_lag1",
    "Unemployment_lag1",
    "IP_Growth_lag1"
]


# ============================================================
# 4. DEFINE TARGET VARIABLES
# ============================================================

target_columns = [
    f"{factor}_next"
    for factor in factor_columns
]


# ============================================================
# 5. DROP MISSING VALUES ONLY NOW
# ============================================================

required_columns = (
    predictor_columns
    + target_columns
)

model_data = model_data.dropna(
    subset=required_columns
).copy()


# ============================================================
# 6. FINAL CHECK
# ============================================================

print("Final model dataset shape:")
print(model_data.shape)

print("\nDate range:")
print(
    model_data.index.min(),
    "to",
    model_data.index.max()
)

print("\nMissing values:")
print(
    model_data[
        required_columns
    ].isna().sum()
)

print("\nDuplicate dates:")
print(
    model_data.index.duplicated().sum()
)

print("\nDates sorted:")
print(
    model_data.index.is_monotonic_increasing
)

# ============================================================
# CORRECT VIF CHECK — INCLUDE CONSTANT
# ============================================================

import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import (
    variance_inflation_factor
)

X_vif = model_data[predictor_columns].copy()

# Add intercept
X_vif_const = sm.add_constant(X_vif)

vif = pd.DataFrame({
    "Variable": X_vif_const.columns,
    "VIF": [
        variance_inflation_factor(
            X_vif_const.values, i
        )
        for i in range(X_vif_const.shape[1])
    ]
})

# Remove constant from displayed results
vif = vif[vif["Variable"] != "const"]

print(
    vif.sort_values(
        "VIF",
        ascending=False
    ).round(3)
)

# ============================================================
# STATIONARITY CHECK — ADF TEST
# ============================================================

from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller
import pandas as pd

adf_results = []

for col in predictor_columns:
    series = model_data[col].dropna()

    result = adfuller(series, autolag="AIC")

    adf_results.append({
        "Variable": col,
        "ADF_Statistic": result[0],
        "p_value": result[1],
        "Stationary_5pct": result[1] < 0.05
    })

adf_results = pd.DataFrame(adf_results)

print(adf_results.round(4))

# ============================================================
# KPSS TEST — CONFIRM BORDERLINE ADF RESULTS
# ============================================================

from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import kpss
import pandas as pd

kpss_results = []

for col in predictor_columns:
    
    series = model_data[col].dropna()

    statistic, p_value, lags, critical_values = kpss(
        series,
        regression="c",
        nlags="auto"
    )

    kpss_results.append({
        "Variable": col,
        "KPSS_Statistic": statistic,
        "p_value": p_value,
        "Stationary_5pct": p_value > 0.05
    })

kpss_results = pd.DataFrame(kpss_results)

print(kpss_results.round(4))

# ============================================================
# TRANSFORM TREASURY 2Y AND UPDATE FINAL PREDICTORS
# ============================================================

# 1. Create monthly change in Treasury 2Y
model_data["Treasury_2Y_change"] = (
    model_data["Treasury_2Y"].diff()
)

# 2. Remove the first observation created as NaN by differencing
model_data = model_data.dropna(
    subset=["Treasury_2Y_change"]
).copy()

# 3. REDEFINE the final predictor list
predictor_columns = [
    "VIX",
    "Credit_Spread",
    "Term_Spread",
    "Treasury_2Y_change",
    "Inflation_lag1",
    "Unemployment_lag1",
    "IP_Growth_lag1"
]

# 4. Check
print("Final predictor variables:")
print(predictor_columns)

print("\nFinal model_data shape:")
print(model_data.shape)

# ============================================================
# FINAL CORRELATION + VIF CHECK AFTER TREASURY TRANSFORMATION
# ============================================================

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

# Correlation
final_corr = model_data[predictor_columns].corr()

print("FINAL PREDICTOR CORRELATION MATRIX:")
print(final_corr.round(3))


# VIF
X_vif = model_data[predictor_columns].copy()
X_vif_const = sm.add_constant(X_vif)

final_vif = pd.DataFrame({
    "Variable": X_vif_const.columns,
    "VIF": [
        variance_inflation_factor(X_vif_const.values, i)
        for i in range(X_vif_const.shape[1])
    ]
})

final_vif = final_vif[
    final_vif["Variable"] != "const"
].sort_values("VIF", ascending=False)

print("\nFINAL VIF:")
print(final_vif.round(3))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error

benchmark_results = []

for target in target_columns:

    # Training historical mean
    historical_mean = train_data[target].mean()

    y_val = validation_data[target]

    # Same forecast for each validation month
    pred = np.repeat(
        historical_mean,
        len(y_val)
    )

    rmse = np.sqrt(
        mean_squared_error(y_val, pred)
    )

    mae = mean_absolute_error(
        y_val,
        pred
    )

    benchmark_results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "Historical_Mean": historical_mean,
        "Validation_RMSE": rmse,
        "Validation_MAE": mae
    })

benchmark_results = pd.DataFrame(
    benchmark_results
)

# ============================================================
# MODELING STEP 4 — Main econometric model: predictive regression (OLS) + Newey-West/HAC
# ============================================================

import statsmodels.api as sm

hac_results = []

for target in target_columns:

    X = model_data[predictor_columns]
    X = sm.add_constant(X)

    y = model_data[target]

    model = sm.OLS(
        y,
        X
    ).fit(
        cov_type="HAC",
        cov_kwds={
            "maxlags": 3
        }
    )

    for variable in predictor_columns:

        hac_results.append({
            "Factor": target,
            "Variable": variable,
            "Coefficient": model.params[variable],
            "HAC_t": model.tvalues[variable],
            "HAC_p": model.pvalues[variable],
            "R_squared": model.rsquared,
            "Adj_R_squared": model.rsquared_adj
        })

hac_results = pd.DataFrame(
    hac_results
)

print(
    hac_results.round(4)
)

# ============================================================
# MODELING STEP 6 — SIMPLE MACRO REGIME CLASSIFICATION
# ============================================================

regime_data = model_data.copy()

vix_median = train_data["VIX"].median()
credit_median = train_data["Credit_Spread"].median()
unemp_median = train_data["Unemployment_lag1"].median()
term_median = train_data["Term_Spread"].median()


def classify_regime(row):

    # Stress regime
    if (
        row["VIX"] > vix_median
        and
        row["Credit_Spread"] > credit_median
    ):
        return "Stress"

    # Expansion-like regime
    elif (
        row["Unemployment_lag1"] < unemp_median
        and
        row["Term_Spread"] > term_median
    ):
        return "Expansion"

    else:
        return "Normal"


regime_data["Regime"] = regime_data.apply(
    classify_regime,
    axis=1
)

print(
    regime_data["Regime"].value_counts()
)

print(
    regime_data.groupby("Regime")[
        [
            "MKT_RF_next",
            "SMB_next",
            "HML_next",
            "RMW_next",
            "CMA_next",
            "MOM_next"
        ]
    ].mean().round(3)
)

# ============================================================
# MODELING STEP 7 — RIDGE / ELASTIC NET
# Time-series-safe hyperparameter tuning
# ============================================================

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import RidgeCV, ElasticNetCV
from sklearn.model_selection import TimeSeriesSplit
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Final predictors and targets
# ------------------------------------------------------------

predictor_columns = [
    "VIX",
    "Credit_Spread",
    "Term_Spread",
    "Treasury_2Y_change",
    "Inflation_lag1",
    "Unemployment_lag1",
    "IP_Growth_lag1"
]

target_columns = [
    "MKT_RF_next",
    "SMB_next",
    "HML_next",
    "RMW_next",
    "CMA_next",
    "MOM_next"
]


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Chronological Train / Validation / Test split
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model_data = model_data.sort_index().copy()

n = len(model_data)

train_end = int(n * 0.60)
val_end   = int(n * 0.80)

train_data = model_data.iloc[:train_end].copy()
val_data   = model_data.iloc[train_end:val_end].copy()
test_data  = model_data.iloc[val_end:].copy()

print("Train:", train_data.index.min(), "to", train_data.index.max(),
      "| N =", len(train_data))

print("Validation:", val_data.index.min(), "to", val_data.index.max(),
      "| N =", len(val_data))

print("Test:", test_data.index.min(), "to", test_data.index.max(),
      "| N =", len(test_data))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. X matrices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

X_train = train_data[predictor_columns]
X_val   = val_data[predictor_columns]
X_test  = test_data[predictor_columns]


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standardize predictors
# IMPORTANT: scaler fitted ONLY on training data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

scaler = StandardScaler()

X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)

X_val_scaled = scaler.transform(X_val)

X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Time-series cross-validation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tscv = TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Hyperparameter grids
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ridge_alphas = np.logspace(-4, 4, 100)

elastic_alphas = np.logspace(-4, 1, 100)

elastic_l1_ratios = [
    0.1,
    0.25,
    0.5,
    0.75,
    0.9,
    0.95
]


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Estimate Ridge and Elastic Net separately for each factor
# ------------------------------------------------------------

results = []

ridge_models = {}
elastic_models = {}

for target in target_columns:

    print("\n========================================")
    print("Target:", target)
    print("========================================")

    y_train = train_data[target]
    y_val   = val_data[target]

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Historical mean benchmark
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    historical_mean = y_train.mean()

    benchmark_pred = np.repeat(
        historical_mean,
        len(y_val)
    )

    benchmark_mse = mean_squared_error(
        y_val,
        benchmark_pred
    )

    benchmark_rmse = np.sqrt(benchmark_mse)

    benchmark_mae = mean_absolute_error(
        y_val,
        benchmark_pred
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # RIDGE
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    ridge = RidgeCV(
        alphas=ridge_alphas,
        cv=tscv
    )

    ridge.fit(
        X_train_scaled,
        y_train
    )

    ridge_pred = ridge.predict(
        X_val_scaled
    )

    ridge_mse = mean_squared_error(
        y_val,
        ridge_pred
    )

    ridge_rmse = np.sqrt(ridge_mse)

    ridge_mae = mean_absolute_error(
        y_val,
        ridge_pred
    )

    ridge_oos_r2 = (
        1 - ridge_mse / benchmark_mse
    )

    ridge_direction = np.mean(
        np.sign(ridge_pred)
        ==
        np.sign(y_val.values)
    )

    ridge_models[target] = ridge


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # ELASTIC NET
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    elastic = ElasticNetCV(
        alphas=elastic_alphas,
        l1_ratio=elastic_l1_ratios,
        cv=tscv,
        max_iter=50000
    )

    elastic.fit(
        X_train_scaled,
        y_train
    )

    elastic_pred = elastic.predict(
        X_val_scaled
    )

    elastic_mse = mean_squared_error(
        y_val,
        elastic_pred
    )

    elastic_rmse = np.sqrt(elastic_mse)

    elastic_mae = mean_absolute_error(
        y_val,
        elastic_pred
    )

    elastic_oos_r2 = (
        1 - elastic_mse / benchmark_mse
    )

    elastic_direction = np.mean(
        np.sign(elastic_pred)
        ==
        np.sign(y_val.values)
    )

    elastic_models[target] = elastic


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Save benchmark
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "Model": "Historical Mean",
        "RMSE": benchmark_rmse,
        "MAE": benchmark_mae,
        "OOS_R2": 0.0,
        "Directional_Accuracy": np.nan,
        "Alpha": np.nan,
        "L1_Ratio": np.nan
    })


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Save Ridge
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "Model": "Ridge",
        "RMSE": ridge_rmse,
        "MAE": ridge_mae,
        "OOS_R2": ridge_oos_r2,
        "Directional_Accuracy": ridge_direction,
        "Alpha": ridge.alpha_,
        "L1_Ratio": np.nan
    })


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Save Elastic Net
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "Model": "Elastic Net",
        "RMSE": elastic_rmse,
        "MAE": elastic_mae,
        "OOS_R2": elastic_oos_r2,
        "Directional_Accuracy": elastic_direction,
        "Alpha": elastic.alpha_,
        "L1_Ratio": elastic.l1_ratio_
    })


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Results table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

step7_results = pd.DataFrame(results)

print("\n")
print("=" * 80)
print("STEP 7 — VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 80)

print(
    step7_results.round(4).to_string(index=False)
)

# ============================================================
# MODELING STEP 8 — EXPANDING WINDOW OOS (Important)
# ============================================================

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

initial_train = int(
    len(model_data) * 0.60
)

oos_results = []

for target in target_columns:

    actual = []
    predicted = []
    dates = []

    for i in range(
        initial_train,
        len(model_data)
    ):

        train = model_data.iloc[:i]

        test = model_data.iloc[
            i:i+1
        ]

        X_train = train[
            predictor_columns
        ]

        y_train = train[target]

        X_test = test[
            predictor_columns
        ]

        model = LinearRegression()

        model.fit(
            X_train,
            y_train
        )

        pred = model.predict(
            X_test
        )[0]

        predicted.append(pred)
        actual.append(
            test[target].iloc[0]
        )
        dates.append(
            test.index[0]
        )

    rmse = np.sqrt(
        mean_squared_error(
            actual,
            predicted
        )
    )

    mae = mean_absolute_error(
        actual,
        predicted
    )

    # Historical-mean benchmark
    benchmark_errors = []

    model_errors = []

    for j in range(
        initial_train,
        len(model_data)
    ):

        hist_mean = (
            model_data.iloc[:j][target]
            .mean()
        )

        actual_j = (
            model_data.iloc[j][target]
        )

        benchmark_errors.append(
            (actual_j - hist_mean) ** 2
        )

        model_errors.append(
            (
                actual[
                    j - initial_train
                ]
                -
                predicted[
                    j - initial_train
                ]
            ) ** 2
        )

    oos_r2 = (
        1
        -
        np.sum(model_errors)
        /
        np.sum(benchmark_errors)
    )

    direction_accuracy = np.mean(
        np.sign(actual)
        ==
        np.sign(predicted)
    )

    oos_results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "RMSE": rmse,
        "MAE": mae,
        "OOS_R2": oos_r2,
        "Directional_Accuracy": (
            direction_accuracy
        )
    })


oos_results = pd.DataFrame(
    oos_results
)

print(
    oos_results.round(4)
)

        Factor    RMSE     MAE  OOS_R2  Directional_Accuracy
0  MKT_RF_next  4.3173  3.3723 -0.0464                0.5230

# ============================================================
# PLACEBO / PERMUTATION FRAMEWORK
# ============================================================

n_permutations = 1000

placebo_scores = []

target = "MKT_RF_next"

for i in range(n_permutations):

    # Shuffle target relationship
    y_permuted = np.random.permutation(
        model_data[target].values
    )

    X = model_data[
        predictor_columns
    ]

    model = LinearRegression()

    model.fit(
        X,
        y_permuted
    )

    score = model.score(
        X,
        y_permuted
    )

    placebo_scores.append(score)

print(
    "Average placebo R2:",
    np.mean(placebo_scores)
)

# ============================================================
# FIGURE 1: HAC Predictive Regression Heatmap
# Color = HAC t-statistic
# Text = regression coefficient + significance
# ============================================================

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Change this only if your dataframe has a different name
df = hac_results.copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Cleaner labels for presentation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

factor_order = [
    "MKT_RF_next",
    "SMB_next",
    "HML_next",
    "RMW_next",
    "CMA_next",
    "MOM_next"
]

variable_order = [
    "VIX",
    "Credit_Spread",
    "Term_Spread",
    "Treasury_2Y_change",
    "Inflation_lag1",
    "Unemployment_lag1",
    "IP_Growth_lag1"
]

factor_labels = {
    "MKT_RF_next": "Market",
    "SMB_next": "SMB",
    "HML_next": "HML",
    "RMW_next": "RMW",
    "CMA_next": "CMA",
    "MOM_next": "Momentum"
}

variable_labels = {
    "VIX": "VIX",
    "Credit_Spread": "Credit Spread",
    "Term_Spread": "Term Spread",
    "Treasury_2Y_change": "Δ 2Y Treasury Yield",
    "Inflation_lag1": "Inflation (t−1)",
    "Unemployment_lag1": "Unemployment (t−1)",
    "IP_Growth_lag1": "IP Growth (t−1)"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create matrices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

t_matrix = (
    df.pivot(index="Variable",
             columns="Factor",
             values="HAC_t")
      .reindex(index=variable_order, columns=factor_order)
)

coef_matrix = (
    df.pivot(index="Variable",
             columns="Factor",
             values="Coefficient")
      .reindex(index=variable_order, columns=factor_order)
)

p_matrix = (
    df.pivot(index="Variable",
             columns="Factor",
             values="HAC_p")
      .reindex(index=variable_order, columns=factor_order)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create significance stars
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def stars(p):
    if p < 0.01:
        return "***"
    elif p < 0.05:
        return "**"
    elif p < 0.10:
        return "*"
    else:
        return ""

annotations = np.empty(coef_matrix.shape, dtype=object)

for i in range(coef_matrix.shape[0]):
    for j in range(coef_matrix.shape[1]):

        coef = coef_matrix.iloc[i, j]
        p = p_matrix.iloc[i, j]

        annotations[i, j] = f"{coef:.2f}{stars(p)}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 7))

limit = max(
    abs(np.nanmin(t_matrix.values)),
    abs(np.nanmax(t_matrix.values))
)

im = ax.imshow(
    t_matrix.values,
    cmap="RdBu_r",
    aspect="auto",
    vmin=-limit,
    vmax=limit
)

# Cell annotations
for i in range(t_matrix.shape[0]):
    for j in range(t_matrix.shape[1]):

        t_value = t_matrix.iloc[i, j]

        text_color = "white" if abs(t_value) > 1.8 else "black"

        ax.text(
            j,
            i,
            annotations[i, j],
            ha="center",
            va="center",
            fontsize=10,
            color=text_color
        )

# Axis labels
ax.set_xticks(range(len(factor_order)))
ax.set_xticklabels(
    [factor_labels[x] for x in factor_order],
    fontsize=11
)

ax.set_yticks(range(len(variable_order)))
ax.set_yticklabels(
    [variable_labels[x] for x in variable_order],
    fontsize=11
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Next-Month Equity Factor Return",
    fontsize=11
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Macroeconomic Predictor",
    fontsize=11
)

# Title
ax.set_title(
    "Macroeconomic Predictors of Next-Month U.S. Equity Factor Returns",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    pad=18
)

# Color bar
cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label(
    "HAC t-statistic",
    rotation=270,
    labelpad=20
)

# Grid between cells
ax.set_xticks(
    np.arange(-0.5, len(factor_order), 1),
    minor=True
)

ax.set_yticks(
    np.arange(-0.5, len(variable_order), 1),
    minor=True
)

ax.grid(
    which="minor",
    linewidth=1
)

ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)

# Notes
fig.text(
    0.5,
    0.01,
    "Cell values are predictive-regression coefficients. "
    "Colors represent HAC/Newey–West t-statistics. "
    "*** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.10.",
    ha="center",
    fontsize=9
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.05, 1, 1])
plt.show()

# ============================================================
# STEP 7C — DIRECTIONAL ACCURACY BENCHMARK
# Compare model accuracy with always predicting the
# most common sign in the training sample
# ============================================================

direction_benchmark_results = []

for target in target_columns:

    y_train = train_data[target]
    y_val = val_data[target]

    # Most common direction in training sample
    positive_share_train = (y_train > 0).mean()

    if positive_share_train >= 0.5:
        benchmark_sign = 1
    else:
        benchmark_sign = -1

    benchmark_accuracy = np.mean(
        np.sign(y_val.values) == benchmark_sign
    )

    direction_benchmark_results.append({
        "Factor": target,
        "Train_Positive_Share": positive_share_train,
        "Validation_Sign_Benchmark": benchmark_accuracy
    })


direction_benchmark = pd.DataFrame(
    direction_benchmark_results
)

print(
    direction_benchmark
    .round(4)
    .to_string(index=False)
)

cbar.set_label(
    "Standardized Elastic Net Coefficient",
    rotation=270,
    labelpad=22
)


fig.text(
    0.5,
    0.01,
    "Zero coefficients indicate predictors removed by Elastic Net regularization. "
    "Predictors were standardized using training-sample information only.",
    ha="center",
    fontsize=9
)


plt.tight_layout(
    rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 1]
)

plt.show()

Elastic Net is applying very aggressive feature selection.

For Market, HML, RMW, and CMA, no macro predictor strong enough to survive the regularization penalty.

For Momentum, it identifies one clear signal of Credit Spread. ighter/stressed credit conditions appear associated with weaker subsequent Momentum performance.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge, ElasticNet, LinearRegression

    "Unemployment_lag1",

]

target_columns = [

    "SMB_next",
    "HML_next",
    "RMW_next",
    "CMA_next",
    "MOM_next"
]

model_data = model_data.sort_index().copy()

n = len(model_data)

train_end = int(n * 0.60)
val_end = int(n * 0.80)

train_data = model_data.iloc[:train_end].copy()
val_data = model_data.iloc[train_end:val_end].copy()
test_data = model_data.iloc[val_end:].copy()

# ============================================================
# STEP 8B — EXPANDING-WINDOW FORECAST LOOP
# ============================================================

forecast_records = []

# First test observation position
test_start_pos = val_end


for target in target_columns:

    print("\n========================================")
    print("Expanding OOS target:", target)
    print("========================================")

    params = frozen_params[target]

    ridge_alpha = params["ridge_alpha"]
    elastic_alpha = params["elastic_alpha"]
    elastic_l1_ratio = params["elastic_l1_ratio"]


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop through every observation in final test period
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for current_pos in range(test_start_pos, len(model_data)):

        current_date = model_data.index[current_pos]

        # --------------------------------------------
        # Estimation sample = everything BEFORE date
        # --------------------------------------------

        expanding_train = model_data.iloc[:current_pos].copy()

        current_row = model_data.iloc[[current_pos]].copy()


        X_train = expanding_train[predictor_columns]
        y_train = expanding_train[target]

        X_current = current_row[predictor_columns]

        y_actual = current_row[target].iloc[0]


        # --------------------------------------------
        # Historical mean benchmark
        # --------------------------------------------

        historical_mean_pred = y_train.mean()


        # --------------------------------------------
        # Standardization
        # Fit scaler only on available history
        # --------------------------------------------

        scaler = StandardScaler()

        X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)

        X_current_scaled = scaler.transform(X_current)


        # --------------------------------------------
        # OLS
        # --------------------------------------------

        ols = LinearRegression()

        ols.fit(
            X_train_scaled,
            y_train
        )

        ols_pred = ols.predict(
            X_current_scaled
        )[0]


        # --------------------------------------------
        # RIDGE
        # Frozen alpha from Step 7
        # --------------------------------------------

        ridge = Ridge(
            alpha=ridge_alpha
        )

        ridge.fit(
            X_train_scaled,
            y_train
        )

        ridge_pred = ridge.predict(
            X_current_scaled
        )[0]


        # --------------------------------------------
        # ELASTIC NET
        # Frozen alpha + L1 ratio from Step 7
        # --------------------------------------------

        elastic = ElasticNet(
            alpha=elastic_alpha,
            l1_ratio=elastic_l1_ratio,
            max_iter=50000
        )

        elastic.fit(
            X_train_scaled,
            y_train
        )

        elastic_pred = elastic.predict(
            X_current_scaled
        )[0]


        # --------------------------------------------
        # Save predictions
        # --------------------------------------------

        forecast_records.append({

            "Date": current_date,
            "Factor": target,

            "Actual": y_actual,

            "Historical_Mean":
                historical_mean_pred,

            "OLS":
                ols_pred,

            "Ridge":
                ridge_pred,

            "Elastic_Net":
                elastic_pred
        })


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Forecast dataframe
# ------------------------------------------------------------

step8_forecasts = pd.DataFrame(
    forecast_records
)

print("\nForecast dataset shape:")
print(step8_forecasts.shape)

print("\nFirst few forecasts:")
print(
    step8_forecasts.head()
)

# ============================================================
# STEP 8C — FINAL PSEUDO-OOS PERFORMANCE
# ============================================================

models = [
    "Historical_Mean",
    "OLS",
    "Ridge",
    "Elastic_Net"
]

step8_results = []


for target in target_columns:

    subset = (
        step8_forecasts[
            step8_forecasts["Factor"] == target
        ]
        .sort_values("Date")
        .copy()
    )

    y = subset["Actual"].values

    benchmark_pred = subset[
        "Historical_Mean"
    ].values

    benchmark_mse = mean_squared_error(
        y,
        benchmark_pred
    )


    for model in models:

        pred = subset[model].values

        mse = mean_squared_error(
            y,
            pred
        )

        rmse = np.sqrt(mse)

        mae = mean_absolute_error(
            y,
            pred
        )


        # --------------------------------------------
        # OOS R2
        # Historical Mean benchmark = 0 by construction
        # --------------------------------------------

        if model == "Historical_Mean":

            oos_r2 = 0.0

        else:

            oos_r2 = (
                1
                -
                mse / benchmark_mse
            )


        # --------------------------------------------
        # Directional accuracy
        # --------------------------------------------

        directional_accuracy = np.mean(
            np.sign(pred)
            ==
            np.sign(y)
        )


        step8_results.append({

            "Factor":
                target,

            "Model":
                model,

            "RMSE":
                rmse,

            "MAE":
                mae,

            "OOS_R2":
                oos_r2,

            "Directional_Accuracy":
                directional_accuracy
        })


step8_results = pd.DataFrame(
    step8_results
)


print("\n")
print("=" * 85)
print("STEP 8 — FINAL EXPANDING-WINDOW PSEUDO-OOS RESULTS")
print("=" * 85)

print(
    step8_results
    .round(4)
    .to_string(index=False)
)

# ============================================================
# FIGURE 8A — FINAL EXPANDING-WINDOW OOS R²
# ============================================================

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


factor_labels = {
    "MKT_RF_next": "Market",
    "SMB_next": "SMB",
    "HML_next": "HML",
    "RMW_next": "RMW",
    "CMA_next": "CMA",
    "MOM_next": "Momentum"
}


plot_results = step8_results[
    step8_results["Model"].isin(
        [
            "OLS",
            "Ridge",
            "Elastic_Net"
        ]
    )
].copy()


r2_matrix = (
    plot_results
    .pivot(
        index="Model",
        columns="Factor",
        values="OOS_R2"
    )
    .reindex(
        index=[
            "OLS",
            "Ridge",
            "Elastic_Net"
        ],
        columns=target_columns
    )
)


r2_matrix.columns = [
    factor_labels[x]
    for x in target_columns
]


r2_matrix.index = [
    "OLS",
    "Ridge",
    "Elastic Net"
]


# Convert to percentage points
r2_percent = r2_matrix * 100


values = r2_percent.values


fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(11, 5)
)


limit = max(
    abs(np.nanmin(values)),
    abs(np.nanmax(values))
)


im = ax.imshow(
    values,
    cmap="RdYlGn",
    aspect="auto",
    vmin=-limit,
    vmax=limit
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Cell labels
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for i in range(values.shape[0]):

    for j in range(values.shape[1]):

        value = values[i, j]

        ax.text(
            j,
            i,
            f"{value:.2f}%",
            ha="center",
            va="center",
            fontsize=11,
            fontweight="bold"
        )


ax.set_xticks(
    range(len(r2_percent.columns))
)

ax.set_xticklabels(
    r2_percent.columns,
    fontsize=11
)


ax.set_yticks(
    range(len(r2_percent.index))
)

ax.set_yticklabels(
    r2_percent.index,
    fontsize=11
)


ax.set_xlabel(
    "Next-Month Equity Factor"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Forecasting Model"
)


ax.set_title(
    "Final Expanding-Window OOS R² Relative to Historical Mean",
    fontsize=14,
    fontweight="bold",
    pad=15
)


cbar = plt.colorbar(
    im,
    ax=ax
)

cbar.set_label(
    "OOS R² (%)",
    rotation=270,
    labelpad=20
)


fig.text(
    0.5,
    0.01,
    "Positive values indicate that the forecasting model reduces mean-squared "
    "forecast error relative to the recursively updated historical-mean benchmark.",
    ha="center",
    fontsize=9
)


plt.tight_layout(
    rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 1]
)

plt.show()

# ============================================================
# FIGURE 8B — CUMULATIVE OOS FORECAST-ERROR ADVANTAGE
# Best-performing model for HML, SMB and CMA
# ============================================================

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


best_pairs = {
    "HML_next": ("OLS", "HML — OLS"),
    "SMB_next": ("Ridge", "SMB — Ridge"),
    "CMA_next": ("OLS", "CMA — OLS")
}


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 6))


for factor, (model, label) in best_pairs.items():

    temp = (
        step8_forecasts[
            step8_forecasts["Factor"] == factor
        ]
        .sort_values("Date")
        .copy()
    )

    # Historical-mean squared error
    benchmark_se = (
        temp["Actual"]
        - temp["Historical_Mean"]
    ) ** 2

    # Model squared error
    model_se = (
        temp["Actual"]
        - temp[model]
    ) ** 2

    # Positive value = model beats benchmark
    advantage = (
        benchmark_se
        - model_se
    )

    cumulative_advantage = (
        advantage.cumsum()
    )

    ax.plot(
        temp["Date"],
        cumulative_advantage,
        linewidth=2,
        label=label
    )


ax.axhline(
    0,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=1
)


ax.set_title(
    "Cumulative Out-of-Sample Forecast-Error Advantage",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    pad=15
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Cumulative Reduction in Squared Forecast Error"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Pseudo-OOS Test Period"
)


ax.legend(
    frameon=False,
    ncol=3
)


ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)


fig.text(
    0.5,
    0.01,
    "Rising values indicate cumulative forecast-error reductions relative "
    "to the recursively updated historical-mean benchmark.",
    ha="center",
    fontsize=9
)


plt.tight_layout(
    rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 1]
)

plt.show()
